The core mathematical structure of CTE involves two interlinked processes: tau protein accumulation and its subsequent spatial spread. Tau accumulation is modeled as a first-order differential equation dependent on impact intensity and time-varying vulnerability. This leads to a progressive neurodegeneration model where pathology spreads beyond initial impact sites even after trauma ceases. Risk is quantified through a weighted sum of head impacts over time, reflecting cumulative exposure rather than isolated events. These models form a dual system: one describing temporal evolution of pathology and another capturing risk assessment. Failure modes arise when thresholds for tau concentration or spread are exceeded, leading to irreversible cognitive decline. The models assume linearity and independence of impact effects, which may not hold under extreme conditions or in heterogeneous populations.
